name: Bootstrap
one_liner: Component-and-grid CSS framework that made responsive layout routine.
what_it_is: A CSS framework shipping pre-built components — navbars, modals, forms, cards — with a responsive grid and utility classes. Recent versions dropped the jQuery dependency and moved the grid onto flexbox and CSS grid.
why_it_matters: Bootstrap solved responsive layout when doing it by hand was genuinely hard, and it is still a sensible choice when you need a working interface faster than you need a distinctive one. Two things changed around it: native flexbox and grid removed the layout problem most teams actually bought it for, and its component styling is recognisable enough that products using it un-customised tend to look like one another. That is a real trade to weigh, not a reason to dismiss it.
suitable_for: Internal tools and admin interfaces where speed beats distinctiveness
Prototypes needing a complete component set immediately
Teams with no design resource who need sane defaults
not_suitable_for: Products with a distinct visual identity, where overriding it can cost more than starting from scratch
Projects that only wanted a grid — native CSS grid covers that now
Bundle-size-sensitive work, unless you are disciplined about importing only what you use
